topStories.headline: Lillie Coit's Finally Opens Its Doors in North Beach After Years of Anticipation
topStories.dek: The French-leaning restaurant at 1707 Powell St. — years in the making in the former Washington Square Bar & Grill space — launched a four-day grand opening October 8–11, bringing a Powell Street closure and a reroute of the 39 Coit bus to the heart of North Beach.
topStories.body:
Lillie Coit's began its four-day grand opening October 8 at 1707 Powell St., with a 7:33 p.m. sign lighting, a Powell Street closure, and a 39 Coit reroute, according to SF News Today and SFMTA. The French-leaning bistro is named for Lillie Hitchcock Coit, the 19th-century San Francisco figure whose bequest funded the construction of Coit Tower atop Telegraph Hill. The restaurant occupies the North Beach building that formerly housed the legendary Washington Square Bar & Grill — known to a generation of Herb Caen readers as the Washbag.

The restaurant is the project of Hole in the Wall Coffee owner Nick Floulis, who has been building toward this opening for years. Before the grand opening, the space operated informally as Petite Lil's, a soft-open bar and kitchen that gave neighborhood regulars and industry insiders an early look. The full restaurant runs as a French bistro with champagne, steak frites, and a late-night kitchen; its decor leans into an Amaro Montenegro theme, with Montenegro-branded water carafes and glassware throughout.

For the grand opening, SFMTA closed Powell Street between Columbus Avenue and Union Street starting at midnight Thursday, October 8, with the closure running through 10 p.m. Sunday, October 11. The 39 Coit outbound bus to Coit Tower was rerouted via Columbus and Union streets to rejoin its regular route; alternate stops are available at Union St. & Columbus Ave., Powell St. & Filbert St., and Union St. & Stockton St.

The opening fell during one of the neighborhood's most compressed weekends of the year — overlapping with the Fleet Week Air Show, Fleet Fest at Fisherman's Wharf, the Italian Heritage Parade, and the Saints Peter & Paul Bazaar. SFMTA's full holiday-week advisory warned that the Powell-Mason Cable Car, Powell-Hyde Cable Car, F Market & Wharves streetcar, and several bus routes would all be rerouted simultaneously across North Beach.

topStories.headline: Two Competing Plans for a North Beach Historic District Pit Preservation Against Housing
topStories.dek: Supervisor Danny Sauter introduced a smaller, locally controlled historic district proposal last week as a counter to a sweeping national nomination that would cover nearly 800 properties across roughly 20 blocks.
topStories.body:
A yearslong battle over how to balance historic preservation and housing construction in San Francisco's landmark-rich North Beach neighborhood took an unexpected turn last week. In response to a broader proposal to establish a national historic district, Supervisor Danny Sauter proposed a much smaller, local district that would also focus on preserving historic buildings — but would, he said, keep more vacant lots, garages, and other empty sites viable for development, according to the San Francisco Chronicle.

The federally recognized district under consideration would include nearly 800 properties, while Sauter has proposed starting with about 200. The national effort — known as the North Beach National Register Historic District — has been championed by the Northeast San Francisco Conservancy and SF Heritage. The nomination, submitted by architectural historian Katherine Petrin, identifies 631 historic contributors: 625 buildings, one site, and five objects, spanning roughly 20 blocks between Russian Hill and Telegraph Hill. If approved, listed properties would automatically appear on the California Register of Historical Resources as well, triggering stricter environmental review for demolition or alteration.

Sauter's legislation, still being drafted, would allow property owners who do not wish to participate in the local district to opt out, according to the Planning Department. "There is no doubt: If any district deserves to be historic, it's North Beach," Sauter said in a statement reported by the Chronicle. "But we can do this in a way that doesn't prevent new housing." He has argued that housing developers could be prevented from using state streamlining laws within a federal historic district, hurting production at a moment when San Francisco is under pressure to build.

The two proposals are proceeding on separate tracks — either could advance independently, both could be approved, or neither could move forward. Sauter told the Chronicle he hopes the State Historical Resources Commission will weigh the existence of a local preservation effort when deciding on the federal nomination. Proponents of the national district have questioned whether Sauter's move is an attempt to thwart their plan. The commission had been poised to hold a hearing on the federal nomination earlier this year before Mayor Daniel Lurie successfully requested a delay for further study.

topStories.headline: Blue Angels, Fleet Fest, and the 158th Italian Heritage Parade All Land on the Northern Waterfront This Weekend
topStories.dek: Fleet Week's signature air show runs Friday through Sunday over the bay, Fleet Fest fills Fisherman's Wharf on Saturday and Sunday, and the Italian Heritage Parade steps off Sunday from Fisherman's Wharf to Washington Square.
topStories.body:
With the congressional budget standoff resolved, this year's 45th annual Fleet Week returned to full scale after a government shutdown forced a heavily scaled-back 2025 event. Fleet Week is in full swing through Monday, October 12, with events concentrated on the northern waterfront. The Parade of Ships took place Friday morning, October 9, from 11 a.m. to noon, with a procession of military ships led by the San Francisco Fire Department sailing into the Bay under the Golden Gate Bridge.

The flagship air show runs Friday, October 9, through Sunday, October 11, from noon to 4 p.m. each day over San Francisco Bay, headlined by the U.S. Navy Blue Angels flying F/A-18 Super Hornets. This year's show is also billed as the only air show in the country featuring a fully choreographed commercial airline performance — a United Airlines Boeing 777. Pier 39 offers excellent sightlines for the aerial displays and the Parade of Ships.

Fleet Fest, the free street festival component of Fleet Week, runs Saturday and Sunday, October 10–11, at Fisherman's Wharf near the SkyStar Wheel and at Pier 27 (9 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day). It features live military band performances, food vendors, public ship tours, and a Service & Safety Expo at Pier 27, with exhibits on military readiness, STEM education, and emergency response. On Sunday, the 191st Army Big Band performs at Fleet Fest at 2 p.m. and the USAF Band of the Golden West plays at Pier 39 at 5 p.m.

Also on Sunday, October 11, the 158th San Francisco Italian Heritage Parade steps off at 12:30 p.m. from the foot of Jefferson and Powell streets in Fisherman's Wharf, marching south along Columbus Avenue to Washington Square in front of Saints Peter and Paul Church. The parade — the longest continuously running Italian Heritage Parade in the United States, dating to 1868 — brings bands, floats, performers, and Italian-American community groups to the streets of North Beach. Actor Joe Mantegna returns as grand marshal. The combined draw of Fleet Week and the parade routinely pushes crowd estimates past 100,000 along the waterfront and Columbus Avenue corridor. SFPD closes parade staging streets as early as 7:30 a.m. Sunday, and SFMTA is running extra F Market & Wharves service along the Embarcadero from Friday through Sunday.

events.title: Fleet Week Air Show: U.S. Navy Blue Angels
events.location: San Francisco Waterfront (Pier 39 and Marina Green offer prime views)
events.description: The Blue Angels headline three days of aerial performances over San Francisco Bay, alongside Heritage Flight formations and a United Airlines Boeing 777 choreographed display. Free to watch from the northern waterfront.

events.title: Fleet Fest at Fisherman's Wharf
events.location: Fisherman's Wharf near the SkyStar Wheel & Pier 27, 2860 Taylor St.
events.description: Free waterfront festival with live military band performances, food vendors, ship tours at Pier 27, and a Service & Safety Expo. The 191st Army Big Band performs Sunday at 2 p.m. and the USAF Band of the Golden West plays Pier 39 at 5 p.m. Free admission.

events.title: 158th San Francisco Italian Heritage Parade
events.location: Jefferson & Powell Sts. (Fisherman's Wharf) to Washington Square, North Beach
events.description: The nation's longest continuously running Italian Heritage Parade marches along Columbus Avenue from Fisherman's Wharf to Washington Square, with bands, floats, and community groups. Grand marshal Joe Mantegna leads. Free; street closures begin at 7:30 a.m.

events.title: Saints Peter & Paul Bazaar
events.time: Saturday 11:00 AM–6:00 PM; Sunday 10:30 AM–5:00 PM
events.location: Saints Peter & Paul School, 666 Filbert St., North Beach
events.description: Annual community bazaar across from Washington Square Park with food, games, rides, and live music. All proceeds benefit Saints Peter and Paul School and the church. Volunteer-run and free to enter.

events.title: San Francisco on Ice — Grand Opening at Fisherman's Wharf
events.location: 80 Jefferson St., Fisherman's Wharf (next to the SkyStar Wheel)
events.description: The city's new 6,300-square-foot outdoor ice rink opens with a ribbon-cutting on November 4. Holds 125 skaters per session; skate rental included with admission. Tickets on sale now at SanFranciscoOnIce.com.

events.title: North Beach First Fridays Art & Culture Walk
events.location: Multiple venues, North Beach (anchor: Grant Ave. & Vallejo St.)
events.description: Monthly self-guided art walk organized by the North Beach Business Association and SF Arts Commission, with more than a dozen galleries, bars, and restaurants open late for art, music, and poetry. Free.

moreNews.headline: San Francisco on Ice Confirms 125-Skater Capacity as Tickets Go on Sale
moreNews.body: Tickets are now on sale for San Francisco on Ice, the 6,300-square-foot outdoor rink opening November 4 at 80 Jefferson St., Fisherman's Wharf, adjacent to the SkyStar Wheel — reported today, October 9, by The Registry SF. The rink can hold 125 skaters per session, and skate rental is included with every admission. Daily hours run 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. through January 18, 2027. A ribbon-cutting ceremony with city officials is set for opening day. Tickets are available at SanFranciscoOnIce.com. The rink will be San Francisco's first new outdoor skating venue since the Embarcadero Center rink closed nearly seven years ago.

restaurants.name: Caffe Trieste
restaurants.description: Founded in 1956 as the first espresso house on the West Coast, this North Beach landmark — where Francis Ford Coppola drafted The Godfather — still serves espresso, pastries, paninis, and live music, celebrating its 70th anniversary in 2026.

restaurants.name: Vesuvio Cafe
restaurants.description: Open since 1948 at 255 Columbus Avenue across from City Lights, this two-floor saloon remains a North Beach institution beloved by writers, tourists, and locals for its Beat-era memorabilia and full bar.

restaurants.name: Mama's on Washington Square
restaurants.description: A family-run North Beach institution since 1964, serving legendary breakfasts and housemade pastries overlooking Washington Square Park, open Tuesday through Sunday.

restaurants.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
restaurants.description: 13-time World Pizza Champion Tony Gemignani's flagship North Beach pizzeria, open since 2009, fires a dozen pizza styles across seven different ovens alongside antipasti, pasta, and a full bar.

restaurants.name: Hilda and Jesse
restaurants.description: A queer-owned, Michelin-starred North Beach dining room specializing in creative brunch and dinner with a playful modern-luxury approach, retaining its star in 2025 and 2026.

restaurants.name: Sotto Mare Oysteria & Seafood
restaurants.description: A beloved North Beach oyster bar and seafood trattoria specializing in house cioppino, fresh oysters, and simply-prepared fish; family-owned and open daily.

restaurants.name: North Beach Restaurant
restaurants.description: A North Beach cornerstone since 1970, renowned for traditional Tuscan-influenced Italian cuisine served in a warm, full-bar dining room on Columbus Avenue.

restaurants.name: Fior d'Italia
restaurants.description: One of America's oldest Italian restaurants, Fior d'Italia offers fine Italian dining with an elegant atmosphere in lively North Beach.

restaurants.name: Flour + Water Pizzeria – North Beach
restaurants.description: The North Beach flagship of Flour + Water Hospitality Group, rooted in the neighborhood's Italian heritage and serving wood-fired pizza on Columbus Avenue.

restaurants.name: Caffe Sport
restaurants.description: A flamboyantly decorated North Beach fixture serving robust Sicilian-influenced pastas, seafood, and garlic-forward sauces in a kitschy interior beloved by longtime regulars.

restaurants.name: Original Joe's
restaurants.description: A North Beach institution famous for its open kitchen, hearty Italian-American plates, steaks, and full bar drawing locals and visitors alike.

restaurants.name: Ideale Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: A warmly-regarded North Beach Italian with Zagat praise and San Francisco Chronicle recognition for its housemade pasta.

restaurants.name: Bocconcino
restaurants.description: A well-reviewed North Beach Italian spot drawing regulars for its pasta and convivial atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Scoma's Restaurant
restaurants.description: A Fisherman's Wharf classic since 1965, Scoma's sits on its own working pier at Pier 47, sourcing Dungeness crab, clam chowder, and sustainable seafood directly from local fishermen pier-to-plate.

restaurants.name: Restaurant Gary Danko
restaurants.description: Open since 1999, this multi-award-winning Fisherman's Wharf destination offers a prix-fixe experience combining classic French technique with local California ingredients, earning consistent Michelin recognition.

restaurants.name: Fog Harbor Fish House
restaurants.description: A family-owned full-bar seafood house on Pier 39 with sweeping Bay views, consistently ranked among the top Fisherman's Wharf restaurants.

restaurants.name: Boudin Bakery & Café
restaurants.description: San Francisco's original sourdough bakery, Boudin serves its famous clam chowder in bread bowls alongside sandwiches and pastries at its flagship Fisherman's Wharf location.

restaurants.name: Eagle Cafe
restaurants.description: A Pier 39 fixture for over 90 years, Eagle Cafe serves hearty American breakfasts and full-bar lunches with an old-wharf feel beloved by early risers and tourists alike.

restaurants.name: The Codmother Fish & Chips
restaurants.description: A beloved Fisherman's Wharf food-truck stand widely praised for some of the best British-style fish and chips in the city.

restaurants.name: Surisan
restaurants.description: A hip, locally-owned Korean fusion brunch spot at Fisherman's Wharf known for its seafood pancakes and modern takes on Korean-American brunch dishes.

restaurants.name: Crab House at Pier 39
restaurants.description: A family-owned Pier 39 seafood restaurant in its 23rd year, specializing in Dungeness crab and Bay shellfish.

restaurants.name: Pier Market Seafood Restaurant
restaurants.description: A family-owned waterfront seafood house on the Fisherman's Wharf promenade offering outdoor seating and classic Bay Area seafood dishes.

restaurants.name: ABACÁ
restaurants.description: A celebrated Filipino-American restaurant at Fisherman's Wharf drawing consistent praise for its creative, seasonal take on Philippine culinary traditions.

restaurants.name: North Beach Cantina
restaurants.description: A Mexican cantina that took over the Stockton Street space in 2022 and has won the neighborhood over with street tacos, fish tacos, and California-style burritos.

restaurants.name: Julius' Castle
restaurants.description: The 1924 Telegraph Hill landmark below Coit Tower, reopening after nearly two decades closed following a restoration of its fire-damaged turret and original wood panelling.

hotels.name: Argonaut Hotel
hotels.description: A Noble House hotel occupying a 1907 brick cannery building on the waterfront, steps from Ghirardelli Square and Pier 39, consistently rated a top Fisherman's Wharf choice.

hotels.name: Hotel Zephyr San Francisco
hotels.description: A playfully designed Fisherman's Wharf hotel with an outdoor courtyard, fire pits, and games, popular for its fun nautical atmosphere and central location.

hotels.name: Hotel Zoe Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A cozy boutique hotel steps from Pier 39, offering comfortable rooms and an on-site restaurant, Pescatore Trattoria.

hotels.name: Hotel Caza Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A well-located 4-star property at the heart of Fisherman's Wharf with a fitness center, pet-friendly rooms, and easy access to the waterfront attractions.

hotels.name: Hotel Riu Plaza Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A 4-star eco-conscious hotel near Pier 39 featuring an outdoor pool, complimentary breakfast buffet, and panoramic city views.

hotels.name: Kimpton Alton Hotel
hotels.description: An IHG boutique hotel with a stylish lobby, pet-friendly policy, and free Wi-Fi, rated highly for its location and service at Fisherman's Wharf.

hotels.name: San Francisco Marriott Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A 4-star Marriott with an on-site restaurant, fitness center, and meeting rooms, conveniently located a short walk from the wharf and Ghirardelli Square.

hotels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
hotels.description: An IHG property offering complimentary breakfast, fitness center, and a central Fisherman's Wharf location within walking distance of major attractions.

hotels.name: Washington Square Inn
hotels.description: A 15-room European-style bed-and-breakfast inn on the edge of Washington Square Park, offering rooms with views of Coit Tower and Saints Peter and Paul Church.

hotels.name: Hotel Boheme
hotels.description: A charming 15-room boutique hotel on Columbus Avenue capturing the bohemian flair of North Beach in the 1950s and 60s, within steps of City Lights and Vesuvio.

shops.name: City Lights Booksellers & Publishers
shops.description: Founded in 1953 by Lawrence Ferlinghetti, this legendary Beat Generation bookstore and publisher specializes in world literature, progressive politics, and poetry, and is a designated San Francisco landmark at 261 Columbus Ave.

shops.name: Molinari Delicatessen
shops.description: Established in 1896, this is San Francisco's oldest Italian deli, famous for its house-made salami sold nationwide, Dutch crunch sandwiches, imported cheeses, and Italian grocery staples.

shops.name: Little Vine
shops.description: A cozy North Beach wine shop beloved for its curated bottle selection, housemade sandwiches, and Thursday-evening wine nights.

shops.name: Libreria Pino
shops.description: A charming independent bookstore and cultural gem tucked into North Beach, earning five-star reviews from its small but devoted following.

shops.name: Cantina Records
shops.description: A North Beach record shop with an eclectic selection of vinyl and an affectionately noted Star Wars figurine collection throughout the space.

shops.name: Macchiarini Creative Design
shops.description: A North Beach institution offering handcrafted jewelry and metalsmithing classes in a working studio open to the public.

shops.name: AB Fits
shops.description: A well-loved North Beach boutique specializing in premium denim and casual wear with a loyal local following.

shops.name: KWAK
shops.description: A one-of-a-kind Pier 39 novelty shop stocking over 600 varieties of rubber ducks, selling more than 50,000 annually and drawing a devoted following.

shops.name: The Shell Cellar
shops.description: A Pier 39 shop with a broad selection of shells, nautical gifts, and sea-themed souvenirs, consistently praised by visitors for its unique inventory.

shops.name: Houdini's Magic Shop
shops.description: A Pier 39 magic shop where staff perform live sleight-of-hand demonstrations and sell tricks, novelties, and illusions for all ages.

artEntertainment.name: Coit Tower
artEntertainment.description: The 210-foot 1933 Art Deco tower atop Telegraph Hill features New Deal murals depicting California life, a free-access base, and a paid elevator to a panoramic observation deck with views of Alcatraz, the Golden Gate, and the Bay.

artEntertainment.name: City Lights Booksellers & Publishers
artEntertainment.description: Beyond its role as a bookstore, City Lights is a San Francisco Designated Landmark (No. 228) and publisher, hosting readings and serving as a living monument to the Beat Generation.

artEntertainment.name: Musée Mécanique
artEntertainment.description: One of the world's largest privately-owned collections of coin-operated mechanical instruments, with over 300 working antique arcade games, player pianos, and automata at Pier 45 — free admission, open 365 days a year.

artEntertainment.name: Aquarium of the Bay
artEntertainment.description: Located at Pier 39, this nonprofit aquarium houses more than 20,000 marine animals native to San Francisco Bay, including sharks, rays, river otters, and jellyfish in 300 feet of glass tunnels.

artEntertainment.name: PIER 39
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's most iconic waterfront destination, featuring two levels of dining, shopping, and attractions alongside the famous free sea-lion colony on K-Dock, with reviews from September 2026 confirming it is in full operation.

artEntertainment.name: Live Worms Gallery
artEntertainment.description: An eclectic North Beach gallery on Grant Avenue giving emerging artists space to exhibit work across diverse media in the heart of the neighborhood.

artEntertainment.name: Paul Thiebaud Gallery
artEntertainment.description: A respected North Beach fine-art gallery representing notable Bay Area artists and hosting rotating exhibitions.

artEntertainment.name: Sweetie's Art Bar
artEntertainment.description: A North Beach neighborhood bar doubling as a gallery space, with local artists' work covering the walls in a relaxed, creative setting.

artEntertainment.name: Telegraph Hill Gallery
artEntertainment.description: A gallery focused on representing contemporary artists and fostering the visual-arts community in the Telegraph Hill neighborhood.

gymsRecreation.name: Bay Club San Francisco
gymsRecreation.description: Open since 1977 as the nation's first co-ed gym, this North Beach flagship offers basketball, squash, pools, yoga, Pilates, and cutting-edge fitness facilities following a recently completed 15,000-square-foot renovation.

gymsRecreation.name: Glow Yoga & Wellness
gymsRecreation.description: A North Beach holistic studio near Washington Square offering yoga, Pilates, barre, kettlebells, yin yoga, sound baths, and an on-site spa with facials, massage, and red light therapy.

gymsRecreation.name: Orangetheory Fitness – North Beach
gymsRecreation.description: A science-backed total-body interval training studio on Columbus Avenue combining strength and cardio workouts led by expert coaches.

gymsRecreation.name: F45 Training North Beach
gymsRecreation.description: A group functional training studio at Northpoint Centre in Fisherman's Wharf offering 45-minute team-based workouts.

gymsRecreation.name: Fit Life Training Studio
gymsRecreation.description: A five-star-rated North Beach boutique training studio with a devoted clientele, praised as an alternative to chain-gym personal training.

gymsRecreation.name: Washington Square Park
gymsRecreation.description: The green heart of North Beach, Washington Square Park hosts morning tai chi, pick-up sports, bocce, and community gatherings surrounded by Saints Peter and Paul Church and neighborhood cafés.

gymsRecreation.name: Coit Tower / Pioneer Park
gymsRecreation.description: The 4.82-acre park crowning Telegraph Hill is free and open daily from 5 a.m. to midnight, offering some of the city's best panoramic views and access to the parrot-inhabited slopes.

gymsRecreation.name: Northpoint Health Club
gymsRecreation.description: A Fisherman's Wharf area health club offering gym facilities and fitness classes to local residents and hotel guests.
